profile.campus: Philadelphia metro, Pennsylvania (Flexential's former Allentown/DC7 building; Flexential's only current active Pennsylvania location is Philadelphia - Collegeville, elsewhere in this registry)
profile.reading:
This facility, previously known as Flexential's DC7 site at 744 Roble Road, Allentown, Pennsylvania, has been vacated by Flexential and is now on the market for lease or sale through a third-party listing agent, Five9s Digital, according to independent Lehigh Valley trade press (IDCNOVA) reporting on the commercial listing. The property was originally built out by InetU, founded around 1996 and acquired by ViaWest in 2015. ViaWest merged with Peak 10 in 2017 to form Flexential in 2018. The current listing describes a single-story, 3.4-acre, 46,800-square-foot facility with a currently installed 2.5 MW of IT capacity, 2.9 MW of backup generation, and 849 kW of UPS capacity, with the listing stating power could reach 10 MW within six months and a full build-out to 40 MW within eight months, supported by PPL Electric Utilities for the expansion. The listing describes leasing as the preferred path for the property over an outright sale. Flexential's own current data center site no longer lists any Allentown or Bethlehem facility. Its only current Pennsylvania location is Philadelphia - Collegeville, elsewhere in this registry. This row is documented here as a former Flexential facility rather than deleted, per registry policy, so the site's history and current market status remain traceable. Pennsylvania's data center market overall trails the major East Coast hubs of Northern Virginia and the New York and New Jersey corridor, with the Lehigh Valley representing a smaller submarket than Philadelphia's own suburbs.

Pennsylvania's data center sales tax exemption, established in 2016 as a refund capped at 5 million dollars and restructured in 2021 into an uncapped exemption with reduced state tracking ability, is now projected by the Shapiro administration to cost 188 million dollars in the 2026-27 fiscal year, rising to 517 million dollars by fiscal year 2031, with total losses since inception potentially reaching about 2 billion dollars by mid-2031, according to Spotlight PA's reporting. Cryptocurrency miners were banned from the program in 2024. State Rep. Greg Vitali introduced a bill to repeal the exemption, but acknowledged uncertain prospects given Governor Shapiro's public support for the program. Shapiro's own budget proposal assumes the exemption continues, with conditional added benefits for developers meeting environmental and employment standards.

reading.body:
This facility in Allentown, Pennsylvania is currently vacant and on the market for lease or sale through a third-party agent after Flexential vacated it in 2026. The listing reports 2.5 MW of installed IT capacity in a 46,800-square-foot building with 2.9 MW of backup generation, and claims expansion potential to 10 MW within six months and 40 MW within eight months with support from PPL Electric Utilities. The operator's published specifications do not disclose what certifications or use cases the facility qualifies for.

If the 40 MW expansion were completed, this site would rank among Pennsylvania's published capacity, but the state's total mapped data center footprint is modest at 22.2 MW across four facilities with published figures and 14 facilities mapped overall. Pennsylvania's data center tax exemption, established in 2016 and restructured in 2021, is projected to cost the state 188 million dollars in 2026-27 and rise to 517 million dollars annually by 2031, with Flexential's own active Pennsylvania presence now limited to one facility in Collegeville.

The Allentown building's expansion timeline and 40 MW build-out claim cannot be verified against Flexential's own specifications because Flexential has left the market there. The expansion would require external validation of power supply commitments from PPL Electric Utilities and actual leasing or purchase activity. Until a new operator takes over or Flexential confirms its departure is permanent, the site's status in Pennsylvania's data center landscape remains speculative.
